sentences.text: This is a Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.9,00,000/ for the death of their Son Master Abhinash who died in a road traffic accident dated 07.05.2022.
SCCH-25 2

. The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, On 07.05.2022 at about 05.45pm, the deceased Master Abhinash was crossing the road near Gurumurthy Temple along with his father, at that time a Cab bearing Reg.No.KA42A8861 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner from Somasundrapalya towards Haraluru and dashed against both Hanamanth Madar and his son.
As a result, they fell on the road, the right side wheel of the Cab ran over the deceased child, due to which Master Abhinash sustained fatal injuries.
Immediately after the accident he was taken to Manipal Hospital, Sarjapura, Bangalore wherein he was declared dead before arriving to the Hospital.
Later PM was conducted at St. John's Hospital at Bangalore and confirmed that the death is caused due to injuries sustained in the accident.
So far they have spent Rs.50,000/ towards transportation and funeral expenses.
SCCH-25 3
. It is the further case of the petitioners that, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 4 years, he was hale and healthy, (Balawadi) Montessori student.
Due to sudden and unnatural death of the child, the petitioners have lost their future dependency, love and affection, company of the deceased and are also facing severe financial problems.
Hence, their lives have become dark and miserable.
The Electronic City Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA42A8861 in Cr.No.0051/2022 p/u/Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC.
Therefore, the 1st Respondent being the owner and the 2nd Respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to them.
Hence, this petition.

sentences.text: In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondents have appeared through their respective counsels, but the respondent No.2 alone filed written statement.
SCCH-25 5.
The objections of the Respondent No.2.
It has contended that the alleged Cab bearing No.KA 42A8861 was not insured with this respondent as on the date of accident.

Further this respondent is not liable to indemnify the insured/owner as he entrusted the vehicle to drive to those who are not having and possessing with valid and effective DL to drive the said Car as on the date of accident.
There is noncompliance of Section 134(C) and Section 158(6) of M.V. Act from the 1st respondent.

Further contended that 1st petitioner was crossing the road along with his deceased son without holding the hand of the minor child on the public road, that too where the pedestrian mark was not there as on the date of accident.
If the 1st petitioner would have taken care of the child on the public road by observing the traffic norms, he could have avoided the accident.
Hence 1st petitioner and deceased have contributed to the accident.

Further contended that in the MLC or police intimation book the vehicle number SCCH-25 has not been mentioned hence, 1st respondent and petitioners colluded and falsely implicated the Cab bearing No.KA42A8861.
Further it has denied the accident, nature of accident, medical expenses.
Further it has contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant, excessive and has no legal basis.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Master Abhinash?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Master Abhinash died on account of road traffic accident took place on 07.05.2022 at about 5.45pm near Gurumurthy Bhavan,
Gurumurthy Temple Road, Somasundrapalya, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Cab bearing Reg.No.KA42A8861?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

from whom?
SCCH-25 4. What Order or Award?
7. In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined the Petitioner No.1 - Sri.Hanamanth Madar who is the father of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.14.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

9. My findings to the above issues are as follows: Issue Nos.1 & 2 : In the affirmative, Issue No.3 :
In the affirmative, SCCH-25 Issue No.4 : As per final order, for the Following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.2: The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA42A8861, have examined the Petitioner No.1 by name Hanamanth Madar i.e., the Father of the deceased as PW.1 and produced 10 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.10.
PW.1 in his examination in chief has reiterated the averments of the petition.
On the other side, the Respondent No.2 has denied the case of the petitioners.
The Respondent No.2/Insurer has not examined any witness including the eye witness who had witnessed the accident or produced any documents.
In the cross examination of PW.1, he has admitted that there was no zebra crossing at the spot of the accident.
However, nothing worthwhile is elicited to disprove the alleged manner of accident and non involvement of the insured vehicle.
The SCCH-25 deceased was only 4 years old and he cannot be at fault as he being a minor cannot be expected to know the traffic Rules.
The driver of the offending vehicle must have taken care and caution while driving the said vehicle which he has not taken as per the police documents.

11. Further, the FIR, FIS, charge sheet, PM report, Inquest mahazar, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar along with Five photos of car, spot sketch, police notice and reply to the notice as per Exs.P.1 to P.10 are public documents which have got presumptive value under law.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the evidence of PW.1 and the documents produced by PW.1 and to accept the version of Respondent No.2.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with documents produced by him, this court is of the opinion that, the driver of the offending vehicle had driven it in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed against the deceased as a result of which deceased had SCCH-25 sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue Nos.1 and 3:
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the Father and the Petitioner No.2 is the Mother of the deceased - Abhinash.
To prove this relationship, the PW.1 has entered into witness box and specifically deposed this relationship in his chiefexamination on oath.
Apart from that, the Petitioners have also produced their Adhar Cards and also Adhar Card of the deceased as per Ex.P.13.
They have also produced Inquest Mahazar as per Ex.P.5, in which the name of the petitioner No.1 is mentioned showing him as father of the deceased.
In Ex.P.13 - Aadhar Card of the deceased, the name of the father of the deceased is mentioned as Hanamanth Madar who is the petitioner No.1 in this case.

Similarly, in the Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.2 - mother of the Hanumanth Madar vs Andanaiah N.K on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155841010/
4 deceased, her husband's name is mentioned as Hanamanth Madar who is SCCH-25 the father of the deceased/petitioner No.1.

sentences.text: In addition the birth certificate at Ex.P.14 also mentions the name of the petitioner No.1 as the father and name of the petitioner No.2 as a mother of the deceased.

These documents are public documents which have got presumptive value under law and have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents and no contrary admission is obtained in the cross examination of PW.1.
The Respondent No.2 has not produced any contrary evidence on record.
As such, there are no reasons to discard these documents produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral and documentary evidence of the Petitioners, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved their relationship with the deceased that the Petitioner No.1 is the Father and the Petitioner No.2 is the Mother of the deceased - Abhinash.
13. While discussing the issue No.2, this Tribunal has come to the conclusion that due to actionable SCCH-25 negligence of the driver of offending vehicle the alleged accident occurred.

Therefore,
under these circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation.

Age of the deceased:
14.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced the Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.13.
As per this document his date of birth is 16.11.2018 and the accident occurred on 07.05.2022.
As such the deceased was 3 years as on the date of accident and from this, it is very clear that as on the date of accident, the deceased was a minor.
Since the deceased was minor as on the date of accident, it shall be deemed that he was not working and not earning anything.
15. Now the quantum of compensation needs to be considered.

The counsel for the petitioners has relied on the decision in the case of 'Kishan Gopal and Anr. Vs. Lala and Ors.' reported in 2013 ACJ 2594 rendered by SCCH-25 Division Bench of Hon'ble Supreme court of India wherein it is held that in case of death of minors, yearly notional income has to be considered at Rs.30,000/ per annum and the age of the youngest parent of the deceased has to be considered for multiplier.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and Anr. Vs. Lala and Ors.' reported in 2013 ACJ 2594
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same principal is applied in Kurvan Ansari Vs. Shyam Kishore Murmu, (2022) 1 SCC 317 and Meena Devi Vs. Nunu Chand Mahto (2023) 1 SCC 204.

sentences.text: As per Ex.P.13 - Aadhar Card of the mother of the deceased by name Manjula Madar (Petitioner No.2) her date of birth is 01.12.1994.
The accident occurred on 07.05.2022.
So, as on the date of accident the age of mother of the deceased was 28 years.
Therefore the proper multiplier applicable to her age is 17.
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.5,10,000/ (Rs.30,000/ X 17 = Rs.5,10,000/).
The Petitioners have claimed that they have spent Rs.50,000/ towards transportation of dead body and towards funeral obsequies.
In this regard they have not produced any documents to show the SCCH-25 expenses.
However, looking into the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be appropriate to award compensation of Rs.20,000/ towards funeral and transportation expenses.
If the deceased was alive certainly he would have saved some amount out of his earnings and created estate in favour of the Petitioners.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under the head of loss to the estate.

Further, in Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his Hanumanth Madar vs Andanaiah N.K on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155841010/
5 family.

With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".
SCCH-25 16.

This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
17.

sentences.text: The Petitioners are the Father and the Mother and they lost their loving and affectionate son at their younger age and they have to live the remaining part of their life without their son.

Therefore,
both are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/ each (Rs.88,000) under the head of loss of consortium.

The counsel for the petitioners has also relied on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Gujarath in Babu Mansa Vs. the Ahemadabad Municipal Corporation report in 1978 ACJ 485, in which it is held that the Tribunal may grant excess amount under a particular head if it finds that the claimants are entitled for higher amount than sought for.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, petitioners have not sought for particular amounts under SCCH-25 particular head so the ratio of this case is not applicable.

As such, in total the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,38,000/ alongwith interest @
6% per annum from the date of petitioner till deposit.

LIABILITY:
18.
The Respondent No.2 has not led any evidence to prove their defence.
Therefore the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
As the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 has to indemnify the 1 st respondent and is directed to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Petitioners claimed an amount of Rs.9,00,000/ but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.6,38,000/.
Hence, the petition is liable to be decreed/allowed.
Accordingly, I answer Issue Nos.1 & 3 in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.4:

In view of the findings on the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH-25 ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.6,38,000/ (Rupee Six Lakhs and Thirty Eight Thousand only) alongwith interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition, till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2/Insurance company is directed to deposit the award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.
SCCH-25
